messages.text:
Review the Infinite Labyrinth project.

The goal is to have a living and fully interactable life-size world built out of 5cm voxels, and visually approaching hand placed/designed games even rivaling games that are not voxel based or proc-gen that's how detailed and intricate I want this engine WHILE maintaining efficiency and the data oriented design philosophy.
This is a game built upon the idea of infinity and not running out of content, about visiting different worlds with completely different genres and aesthetics, and each world needs to be fully fleshed out, each world needs to be a modern (April 2026) minecraft/barony/starbound/fallout/borderlands/D&D self contained whole.
This is an omniversal game, let's do real research into making this a reality.

And let's not stop at just emulating minecraft and other voxel games like what can we do better? What can we do with the math and code to really innovate?

Shawn, this is a massive and exciting research task. You've given me a crystal-clear vision — 5cm voxel fidelity at life-size scale, visually rivaling hand-crafted non-voxel games, infinite genre-spanning worlds each as deep as a standalone title, all on top of your existing ECS/SDF architecture. Let me dive deep into the cutting edge of voxel engines, SDF rendering, procedural generation, data-oriented design, and where the real innovation frontiers are in 2026.

Launching the deep dive now.

Your voxel engine technical research compendium is ready. It covers data structures (SVDAGs vs. octrees vs. 64-trees), rendering pipelines (ray marching, greedy meshing, SDF), global illumination approaches (Radiance Cascades, VCT, SDFGI), procedural generation strategies (WFC, climate noise, AI-assisted PCG), performance architecture (Arch ECS, chunk sizing, C# optimization), and hardware budgets for 2026 consumer GPUs. The report synthesizes findings from Teardown, Aokana, John Lin's engine, and academic publications through May 2025, with specific architectural recommendations for building a 5cm-voxel omniversal engine.
